args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18). Action taken: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Post-rollback status: v2.3.0 in all regions, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 is marked unhealthy in production; v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. No change-manager approval was needed because v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure before any redeploy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened a SEV2 incident. The on-call engineer has been paged.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an error rate of 0.18. v2.3.0 was the most recent production release that was healthy, so I used it. It had already run healthy in production, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Current state:** checkout-api is healthy on v2.3.0 in every region, with an error rate of 0.002.
- **Incident:** It is open at SEV2 and titled "checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0". The summary records the rollback, the post-rollback status, and that v2.3.1 needs investigation before any redeploy.

content.text: The most recent production release that was healthy is v2.3.0 (v2.2.9 is older). v2.3.1 is the unhealthy one, and v2.3.0 has already run healthy in production, so no change-manager approval is needed. Rolling back to v2.3.0 now.
The rollback worked and checkout-api is healthy again. Now I'll open the SEV2 incident.
